displayName: PHP / Magento → Java 21 · Spring Boot 3  OR  .NET 8
description: PHP (Tier-4, incl. Magento-style storefronts) migrating to a strongly-typed managed target — the SME picks Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 OR .NET 8 per routine (compatibleTargetStacks lists both). The claim taxonomy is target-agnostic; each extract prompt (php/java-spring, php/dotnet8) supplies the language-specific mapping. PHP's idiom gap to a static language is dominated by its dynamic type system: loose equality / type juggling (== vs ===, "0" == false, numeric-string coercion), the array-as-ordered-map (a single type doing duty as both list and dictionary), null/absence semantics (isset / empty / ?? / the @ error-suppression operator, undefined-variable-is-null), superglobal request state ($_GET / $_POST / $_SESSION / $_SERVER) that couples code like hidden globals, and Throwable/@-suppression error handling. Unlike ABL, PHP has a free/OSS runtime, so source-execution equivalence is technically FEASIBLE via a php-sidecar (run the source, compare outputs) — but that sidecar is not built yet, so it is NOT claimed here; verification currently rests on golden-dataset extraction scoring plus compile + invariant-execution of the generated target.

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants the function must preserve across all valid inputs — the business rules a reviewer signs off on and the Java/.NET target must uphold.

claimKinds.label: Loose type coercion / juggling
claimKinds.description: PHP's loose equality (==) and type juggling: "0" == false, 0 == "" (pre-8), "1e2" == "100", numeric-string vs string comparison, implicit string↔number coercion in arithmetic and conditionals. PHP 8 tightened some of these (0 == "abc" is now false), so the PHP VERSION matters. The migration must choose an EXPLICIT typed comparison in Java/.NET — the trap is that a naive translation to == / .equals() changes truthiness. Flag the exact juggling and the intended strict semantics.

fields.name: expression
fields.doc: The PHP expression, e.g. 'if ($qty == false)' or '$a == $b' where $a is a numeric string.

fields.name: php_version_sensitive
fields.doc: Whether the result changed between PHP 7 and PHP 8 (e.g. 0 == "abc").

fields.name: target_semantics
fields.doc: The explicit typed comparison the Java/.NET target must use, e.g. 'compare as int after validating the string is numeric', or 'use === → .equals with same type'.

claimKinds.label: Array shape semantics
claimKinds.description: The PHP array is a single ordered-map type doing duty as BOTH a list and a dictionary, and often both at once (mixed integer + string keys). The migration must resolve which each usage is: a sequential 0..n array ⟶ List / List<T>; an associative array ⟶ LinkedHashMap / Dictionary (order-preserving); a mixed/record shape ⟶ a DTO / record. Also capture array-function semantics that don't map 1:1 (array_merge renumbers integer keys, + does not; sort resets keys; foreach preserves insertion order).

claimKinds.label: Null / absence contract
claimKinds.description: PHP's absence semantics, which are subtle and lossy: an undefined variable or missing array key reads as null (with a notice/warning, not an error); isset() is false for null AND unset; empty() is true for null, 0, "", "0", [], false (a frequent bug — empty("0") is TRUE); ?? (null-coalescing) suppresses the undefined notice; ?-> (nullsafe) short-circuits; and the @ operator silently suppresses errors on any expression. The target must make each of these an EXPLICIT nullable / Optional with the correct default, and must NOT conflate empty() with null.

fields.name: target_pattern
fields.doc: e.g. 'Optional<T> with orElse(default)' / 'nullable + explicit != null check', noting the empty() vs null distinction.

claimKinds.label: Superglobal / request state usage
claimKinds.description: Direct reads/writes of PHP superglobals — $_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_SESSION, $_COOKIE, $_SERVER, $_FILES, $GLOBALS — which couple business logic to ambient request/session state exactly like a global variable (no parameter passing). These have NO equivalent in a Java/.NET service and are a security + testability trap. The migration must lift them to an EXPLICIT injected boundary: a request DTO / @RequestParam / bound model for inputs, and a request-scoped session bean for $_SESSION — never ambient static state. Writing a superglobal (e.g. $_SESSION['cart'] = ...) is also a side effect.

fields.name: target_binding
fields.doc: e.g. 'a @RequestParam int qty (validated)' / 'a request-scoped SessionCart bean'.

claimKinds.label: Error handling contract
claimKinds.description: PHP error handling spans several mechanisms that must all become typed exceptions: try/catch on Throwable (Exception + Error since PHP 7), the @ error-suppression operator (silently swallows warnings/errors on an expression — a latent-bug trap, classify as 'suppressed'), trigger_error / set_error_handler, and functions that signal failure by returning false (e.g. file_get_contents, json_decode) rather than throwing. The target uses try/catch + typed exceptions; every @-suppression and every false-return-on-failure must be classified checked vs swallowed.

fields.name: swallowed
fields.doc: Whether the failure is silently swallowed with no follow-up check (a likely latent bug).

claimKinds.label: Side effect
claimKinds.description: Externally-visible state mutations: database writes, output (echo / print / rendering), HTTP headers (header(), setcookie()), superglobal / $_SESSION mutation, file I/O (fopen / file_put_contents), external calls (curl), and mail(). Rendering/echo in the middle of business logic is a classic PHP concern-mixing trap the migration must separate.

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Boundary and semantic conditions specific to PHP → Java/.NET: float precision (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3; money must be a decimal type, never a float); integer overflow silently promotes to float; intval()/(int) truncates and parses leading digits ((int)"5 apples" == 5, (int)"0x1A" == 0 in PHP 7+); string increment ('a'++ == 'b', '9'++ == '10'); switch uses loose (==) matching; and the ternary/?? associativity quirks. Each must be reproduced with the correct typed behaviour.

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Ambiguities that require SME resolution. Common PHP/Magento cases: Magento framework coupling (the DI container / ObjectManager, plugins & interceptors, layout XML, the EAV data model, module config) has no direct target equivalent and must be re-platformed deliberately; magic methods (__get/__set/__call/__toString) and dynamic properties; variable variables ($$name) and variable function/method calls; dynamic include/require and eval(); and the physical DB schema behind raw SQL or an ORM.

topLevelFields.name: enclosing_type
topLevelFields.doc: The enclosing class/trait, or the .php file basename for a free function.

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: PHP parameter modes. Default = by value; &$x = by reference (input-output); return = the return value; superglobal = an ambient $_GET/$_POST/$_SESSION input the target must lift to an explicit parameter.

promptHints.emphasis: Every == / != (loose) comparison is a looseTypeCoercion candidate — note whether PHP 8 changed it and give the strict typed target semantics. Every array is an arrayShapeSemantics claim — decide list vs map vs record. isset/empty/??/@ and undefined reads are nullSafetyContract claims; NEVER conflate empty() with null (empty("0") is true). Every $_GET/$_POST/$_SESSION/$_SERVER touch is a superglobalUsage claim (hidden request/session coupling → explicit injected boundary). Every @ suppression and every false-on-failure return is an errorHandlingContract; classify swallowed vs checked. Treat money-as-float, int overflow→float, (int) truncation, and loose switch as edgeCase claims. Magento DI/plugins/EAV, magic methods, and dynamic include/eval are openQuestions.

calibratedAgainst: PHP language reference (type juggling, arrays, superglobals, PHP 7→8 comparison changes)
